nodes.label: Public education

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Waste reduction strategies|Public education_qna_000
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: What local knowledge institutions and practices were identified for sustainable waste management in the study?
nodes.answer: The practices identified include social cooperation, taboos, local chief's pronouncements, and the conversion of household solid waste into assets.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Waste reduction strategies|Public education_qna_001
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What did the study advocate for in terms of waste management planning?
nodes.answer: The study advocated for the integration of local knowledge and the informal sector into the greater waste management planning system.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Waste reduction strategies|Public education_qna_002
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What is the significance of local knowledge in waste management practices according to the study?
nodes.answer: Local knowledge is significant as it informs waste management practices that are crucial for supporting ecological system sustainability.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Waste reduction strategies|Public education_qna_003
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: How will this study contribute to waste management solutions?
nodes.answer: The study will add to the inventory of accessible, user-relevant solutions to waste management and will be available in libraries for policymakers and community leaders.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Waste reduction strategies|Public education_qna_004
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What does the new knowledge add to for practitioners regarding waste management?
nodes.answer: The new knowledge adds to the inventory of sustainable waste management practices available to local communities.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Waste reduction strategies|Public education_qna_005
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: What do the literature reviews highlight about local knowledge in waste management?
nodes.answer: The literature reviews highlight the relevance of local knowledge in solid waste management in sub-Saharan Africa.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Waste reduction strategies|Public education_qna_006
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What is the significance of municipalities offering waste education programs in reducing litter on coasts?
nodes.answer: Studies have shown that municipalities offering waste education programs can lead to decreased litter on coasts, as increased citizen knowledge on waste management practices helps in promoting responsible behaviours towards plastics disposal.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Waste reduction strategies|Public education_qna_007
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What strategy could be effective in influencing Waste Laggards to engage in sustainable behaviours?
nodes.answer: For some individuals in this group, raising awareness, triggering environmental values, and increasing knowledge may be effective in encouraging them towards sustainable behaviours.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Waste reduction strategies|Public education_qna_008
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: How does income level affect engagement in pro-environmental behaviours?
nodes.answer: Older respondents and those with higher income tend to show higher engagement in pro-environmental behaviours, such as waste minimization behaviour, as found in studies (European Commission, 2017; Barr, 2003).
